title: QCLI-432 confirmatory-check minors: guide and help omit the lone-state carve-out, the T-3 comment overstates, and identity is unasserted at the CLI layer
description:
Four minor findings from QCLI-432's DEC-172 (4ab) confirmatory review (opum-control review seq 7991, head aeab619a1a489b99cbec0eb000eee5a0d038bb27), none blocking, filed together as one follow-up:

(1)+(2) The task-creation guide (src/application/agents/guides.ts, refs-aware section) and the `task list --across-refs` help (src/application/command-help.ts) describe `identity` without stating the lone-state carve-out: the code returns `task` for ANY group with fewer than two states regardless of createdAt (src/application/refs/across-refs.ts). Read literally, a one-state group with no createdAt matches the `unresolved` clause -- the opposite of the code and of the lone-state test. Both surfaces name only the pair case.

(3) The comment on the T-3 assertion (test/qcli417-across-refs.test.ts) says 'a lone state has nothing to collide with, so it is one task whatever its record carries', but T-3 is created with `quest task create` and so carries a createdAt; removing the guard leaves T-3 green. The lone-no-createdAt property is pinned by the T-9 test, not the assertion this comment annotates.

(4) `identity` is asserted only through the service view(); no test reads it back through the CLI JSON envelope of `task list --across-refs`. AC1 is about what the command reports, and the command layer is unpinned for this field.

Filed by the quest-cli worker at team-lead instruction; UNSTAMPED.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The task-creation guide and the `task list --across-refs` help both state that a lone state (a group of fewer than two states) is always `task`, so a literal reading does not misclassify a lone record with no createdAt as `unresolved`

A test asserts `identity` through the CLI JSON envelope of `task list --across-refs`, not only through the service view()

finalSummary:
Three QCLI-432 confirmatory-check minors, fixed together.

AC1: src/application/agents/guides.ts (the refs-aware section of the task-creation guide) and the `task list --across-refs` help in src/application/command-help.ts now both state the lone-state carve-out the code implements -- a group of fewer than two states is always `task`, whatever its record carries, so a one-state group with no createdAt is `task` and not `unresolved`. Both surfaces previously named only the pair case, so a literal reading misclassified the lone case.

AC2: the comment on the T-3 assertion in test/qcli417-across-refs.test.ts is scoped to what that assertion demonstrates. T-3 is a PR-head-only record built with `quest task create`, so it carries a createdAt and the assertion cannot show the carve-out's finer half; the comment now attributes the lone-no-createdAt property to the T-9 test that actually pins it, and says that is the case that goes red if the `states.length < 2` guard is removed.

AC3: added a test that asserts `identity` through the CLI JSON envelope of `task list --across-refs`, not only through the service view(). Over the fixture's colliding PR head it asserts T-1 is `collision` on the envelope, with T-2 as `task` the negative control that stops the assertion passing against a constant.

Proven both ways (AC3): with the test in place, forcing identityOf to a constant (`collision` -> `task`) turns the envelope assertion red -- "Expected: collision / Received: task". The mutation was reverted with `git checkout`, so src/application/refs/across-refs.ts is byte-identical to dev; the delivered source change is the two wording files only.

Verified: the whole qcli417 file is green (41 pass / 0 fail); `biome check` is clean on all three changed files; `quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude` still exits 0 (the guide edit does not disturb the managed block); `bun run check` exits 0 on the declared bun 1.4.2.
